explanations: terra: The covenant joins worship of Allah with good conduct toward orphans and other dependents, placing care for the orphan inside a binding relational duty.

terra: The Prophet is warned that other communities will never be satisfied with him until he follows their way; satisfaction here exerts directional pressure, and revelation sets a boundary against yielding to it.

luna: The section says the Prophet’s rida is granted through a direction; 2:144 names God’s seeing his face turn toward heaven and promises a qibla تَرْضَاهَا. It makes the inward satisfaction visible as an answered bodily orientation. | terra: Allah sees the Prophet repeatedly turning his face skyward and turns him toward قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا; an observed orientation is answered by a gift of direction that pleases him.

luna: The section’s secondary dictionary gloss for و ج د includes الحب; this verse says believers are أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ, making love an intense orientation toward God. It clarifies the love pole against the section’s شدة البغض, though it is a different relationship and object.

luna: The section’s secondary dictionary gloss for و ج د is الحب; 2:177 says to give wealth عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ to orphans among others. It directly joins love to material care for the vulnerable person whom the section says was sheltered. | terra: True righteousness includes giving cherished wealth to orphans and other vulnerable people, making love of possession yield to material care.

luna: The section says رضى can be reached through effort; 2:207 describes a person who offers himself seeking Allah’s pleasure (ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاتِ اللَّهِ). It gives the reverse movement: a servant strives for the Lord’s رضى. | terra: Selling oneself while seeking Allah's pleasure is an extreme instance of rida pursued through effort and directed toward God, rather than a mood that simply arrives.
terra: People may hate what is good for them and love what is bad for them, a direct warning that emotional direction does not by itself establish the worth of its object.

luna: The section’s qahr gloss warns against taking from an orphan without consent; 2:220 says that setting their affairs right is best and allows shared household dealings when they are treated as brothers. It distinguishes responsible care from exploitative separation or use. | terra: Reform is named as the right purpose in handling orphans, who are called brothers; the ayah replaces domination with relational care while warning that Allah knows corrupter from reformer.
terra: Guardians must not prevent former spouses from remarrying when they mutually agree honorably; تَرَاضَوْا بَيْنَهُم makes reciprocal rida a protection against coercive control.

luna: The section says رضى can be mutual and that an orphan must not be coerced; 2:233 allows parents to wean a child by mutual agreement and consultation, then discusses arranging a wet nurse and payment fairly. It joins consent to tender care of a dependent child. | terra: Parents may decide weaning عَن تَرَاضٍ مِّنْهُمَا وَتَشَاوُرٍ; this is literal two-party satisfaction governing care for a dependent child and excluding unilateral force.
terra: The declaration that there is no compulsion in religion supplies a broad but explicit boundary between coerced submission and willing heart-direction.
terra: Spending wealth in pursuit of Allah's pleasure and inner firmness connects effort, giving, and a heart-set direction to rida.
terra: Gardens, purified spouses, and Allah's satisfaction are offered as what is better than worldly desires, joining bestowed reward with rida and the latter-over-former contrast.
terra: Love of Allah is tested by following the Prophet, after which Allah loves and forgives, giving love an enacted route and a reciprocal answer.

luna: The section traces an emotional direction away from aversion toward رضى; 3:103 recalls people who were enemies until God brought their hearts together and made them brothers. It depicts the same reversal at the level of a community. | terra: Former enemies become brothers when Allah joins their hearts and rescues them from a brink; this is a divinely effected reversal in the direction of human feeling.

luna: The section’s secondary dictionary note for و ج د includes anger toward a person; 3:119 depicts people biting their fingertips in fury at believers. This gives a specific human hostility that contrasts with the reassurance that God did not reject the Prophet; the verse uses غيظ, not the section’s root.
terra: The God-conscious restrain anger and pardon people, converting a strong hostile feeling into merciful conduct toward its possible object.

luna: The source section’s ء و ي note describes a heart softening in pity; here God’s mercy makes the Prophet gentle to people (لِنتَ لَهُمْ), while a harsh, hard heart would scatter them. This shows tenderness as the social opposite of rejection. | terra: Divine mercy makes the Prophet gentle; hardness of heart would scatter people, while pardon and consultation enact the tender turn toward them that the āwā dictionary sense describes.

luna: The section defines ر ض و as the opposite of displeasure; 3:162 asks whether one who follows Allah’s رضوان is like one who incurs His سَخَط. It states the boundary between following divine approval and meeting its opposite. | terra: The ayah asks whether one who follows Allah's pleasure can be like one who incurs His anger, giving the lexicon's rida-versus-sakhat opposition an explicit moral form.
terra: The believers follow Allah's pleasure after fear and return with bounty untouched by harm, making rida the chosen direction of a difficult response.

luna: The section says not to oppress an orphan or take from him without consent; 4:2 commands giving orphans their property and forbids consuming it by mixing it with one’s own. It makes protection of the orphan’s own wealth a concrete form of care. | terra: The command to give orphans their property and never consume it into one's own directly specifies what refusing to overpower an orphan means in material dealings.
terra: Fear of failing to act justly toward orphan girls changes what marriages are permitted, so adult desire is explicitly bounded by the vulnerable orphan's right to justice.

luna: The section defines ق ه ر as taking something without a person’s consent; 4:4 says a wife may remit part of her bridal gift and it may be received only when she gives it willingly. It makes voluntary consent the boundary between a gift and taking.

luna: The section links not coercing an orphan to a person who has been brought to رضى; 4:6 orders guardians to test orphans at maturity and hand over their property when sound judgment appears. It shows the promised return of control to the person whose assets were held. | terra: Guardians must test orphans, deliver their wealth at maturity, avoid consuming it wastefully, and call witnesses; the ayah turns non-coercive care into an accountable practice.

terra: When orphans and other vulnerable people attend an estate division, they must be provided from it and addressed kindly; property distribution is joined to tender speech rather than overpowering exclusion.

luna: The section’s dictionary gloss for ق ه ر is coercive taking without consent; 4:10 condemns consuming orphan property unjustly, even describing it as eating fire. It names the material harm that the prohibition on dominating an orphan excludes. | terra: Consuming orphan wealth unjustly is described as consuming fire, stating the consequence of the taking-without-rida that the section draws from qahr.

luna: The section’s dictionary explanation of ق ه ر is taking without the person’s consent; 4:19 forbids inheriting women against their will (كَرْهًا) and commands decent treatment. It gives a concrete boundary against coercion, parallel to not dominating an orphan. | terra: The prohibition on inheriting women against their will or constraining them to recover gifts precisely opposes acquisition without the other person's rida.
terra: After the required marital due, mutually agreed adjustment carries no blame; تَرَاضَيْتُم makes consent, effort, and material giving a two-sided relation.

luna: The section glosses ق ه ر as taking by force without the other person’s consent and says رضى can be mutual; this verse bars wrongful consumption of one another’s wealth and allows trade عَن تَرَاضٍ مِّنكُمْ. It states the consent boundary that distinguishes exchange from coercive taking. | terra: The ban on consuming one another's property permits trade only عَن تَرَاضٍ مِّنكُمْ, directly clarifying the section's move from qahr as taking without consent to rida as the condition for taking.
terra: Kind treatment of orphans is included among the concrete human relations that must follow exclusive worship, extending received divine care into care of dependents.

terra: True submission requires that people find no inner resistance to the Prophet's judgment; لَا يَجِدُوا فِي أَنفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا makes finding an inward state and distinguishes willing acceptance from coerced compliance.
terra: Charity, recognized good, and reconciliation become greatly rewarded when done seeking Allah's pleasure, showing concrete labor undertaken to attain rida.

luna: The section says the orphan must not be subjected to قهر; 4:127 commands standing for orphan women with justice and names rights withheld from them in marriage/property matters. It shows oppression can be neglect of their claims as well as forceful seizure. | terra: The ruling on orphan girls condemns withholding what is prescribed for them while desiring marriage and commands justice for vulnerable children, exposing how desire must be bounded by their rights.
terra: Pilgrims are described as seeking bounty and satisfaction from their Lord, another concrete pairing of active pursuit, divine giving, and rida.
terra: Allah says that He has approved Islam as religion for the believers, using rida as divine acceptance directed toward a way rather than as affection indiscriminately directed toward persons.
terra: Hatred of a people must not turn the believers away from justice; this directly bounds how loathing may be directed and what conduct may follow from it.
terra: Allah guides those who follow His pleasure into paths of peace, making rida an orientation that produces guidance and movement out of darkness.

luna: The section’s secondary dictionary gloss for و ج د includes love; 5:54 describes a people whom God loves and who love Him, humble toward believers and firm toward disbelievers. It makes love reciprocal and shows that its expression changes with its object. | terra: Allah brings a people whom He loves and who love Him, a reciprocal love relation that parallels the reciprocal rida formula while directing their stance differently toward believers and rejecters.

terra: لَتَجِدَنَّ frames a finding about emotional direction: some people are found most intense in enmity while others are nearest in affection, allowing the w-j-d root to carry sharply opposed heart-relations.

luna: The section names the two-sided state of رضى; 5:119 repeats that Allah is pleased with them and they with Him after naming the truthful and their reward. It locates mutual approval at the outcome of the judgment. | terra: After truthfulness receives its lasting reward, رَّضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ makes mutual satisfaction the relation between the giver of the gardens and their recipients.
terra: Allah alone is الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ; divine irresistible sovereignty marks the boundary around the human command not to use qahr against an orphan.

luna: The section’s ء و ي note describes a heart turning toward and softening for someone; 6:52 tells the Prophet not to drive away those who call on their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face. It makes welcoming the low-status worshiper a concrete counterpart to sheltering the orphan.
terra: The repeated title الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ places qahr at the level of divine rule and guardianship, not a license for a powerful human over the vulnerable.

luna: The section’s ق ه ر note highlights taking without the orphan’s consent; 6:152 says not to approach an orphan’s property except in the best manner until maturity. It states the protective limit on a guardian’s power. | terra: The orphan's property may be approached only in the best manner until maturity, a precise boundary against the taking-without-rida evoked by the section's definition of qahr.
terra: Allah removes rancor from the garden-dwellers' breasts as they acknowledge that divine guidance brought them to the granted garden, linking inward cleansing with received reward.

luna: The section’s dictionary gloss of ق ه ر is coercive taking without consent; 7:127 has Pharaoh’s people announce their domination over the Israelites while planning to kill their sons and spare their women. It gives the violent, powerful sense of the named root that the orphan command forbids.

luna: The section’s root ء و ي is used for God sheltering an orphan; here the believers recall being few and oppressed, fearing capture, when God gave them refuge (فَآوَاكُمْ), support, and provision. The parallel makes refuge a response to vulnerability. | terra: Allah reminds an exposed, fearful community that He sheltered them, strengthened them, and gave good provision so they might be grateful; فَآوَاكُمْ expands the orphan's shelter into communal divine care.
terra: Allah joins the believers' hearts in a way no expenditure of all earthly wealth could have achieved, showing the heart's turn as a divine gift beyond human effort or payment.

luna: The section’s dictionary note on ء و ي includes taking someone in; 8:72 names the believers who gave refuge (آوَوا) and aid to emigrants, making shelter a concrete duty toward people forced from home and joining it to mutual protection. | terra: The believers who آوَوا and supported the emigrants turn shelter into a human act of loyalty, echoing divine shelter and the heart's compassionate turn in the section.

luna: The section’s ء و ي image is shelter offered to someone vulnerable; 8:74 repeats the emigrants and their hosts who gave refuge (آوَوا) and aid, then calls them true believers and promises forgiveness and noble provision. It shows the spiritual weight of receiving the displaced. | terra: Those who believed, emigrated, sheltered, and supported are called true believers and promised provision, joining enacted refuge with a favorable divine response.
terra: A polytheist who seeks protection must be sheltered and then conveyed to safety; compassion and refuge are required even toward someone outside the community and potential hostility.
terra: Allah removes rage from believers' hearts and turns mercifully toward whom He wills, a direct divinely caused alteration of the heart's hostile state.
terra: Allah gives believers glad tidings of mercy, satisfaction, and lasting gardens, presenting divine rida together with promised gifts to their recipients.

luna: The section’s secondary dictionary gloss for و ج د includes love and frames the heart’s changing direction; 9:24 lists family, acquired wealth, trade, and homes as attachments that can be preferred over God, His Messenger, and striving in His path. It gives a concrete boundary for where love is directed.
terra: أَرَضِيتُم بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ rebukes satisfaction directed to the nearer life over the hereafter, reversing the surah's claim that the latter is better than the former.

luna: The section defines ر ض و as the opposite of displeasure; 9:58 contrasts people pleased when given from the charity and angered when not (إِذَا هُمْ يَسْخَطُونَ). The response to a gift makes the section’s turn from displeasure to satisfaction concrete, with its reversal exposed. | terra: The response to distribution is stated in the section's exact sequence and opposition: when they are given they are pleased, and when they are not given they become angry; أُعْطُوا ... رَضُوا and يَسْخَطُونَ expose a corrupt version of gift producing satisfaction.

luna: The section’s root ر ض و links giving to the recipient’s satisfaction; 9:59 says they would be satisfied with what Allah and His Messenger gave them (رَضُوا بِمَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ) and trusts Allah’s further bounty. It closely parallels gift followed by رضى. | terra: This supplies the rightly directed alternative to 9:58: being content with what Allah and His messenger give would turn reception into trust and desire toward Allah, precisely the gift-to-rida movement of فَتَرْضَىٰ.

luna: The section links divine giving with the recipient’s رضى; 9:72 lists gardens and dwellings for believing men and women, then says Allah’s رضوان is greater. It presents divine approval itself as the greatest gift. | terra: After gardens and lasting dwellings are promised, Allah's rida is called greater; the emotional relation exceeds the gifts that accompany it even while those gifts lead into it.
terra: They are content to remain with those left behind and their hearts are sealed; rida becomes a chosen lowering of action rather than the fruitful response to divine giving.

terra: Those unable to join turn away with eyes overflowing in grief because they cannot find anything to spend; يَجِدُونَ and حَزَنًا occur together, explicitly joining the root's ordinary 'find' sense to its dictionary face of grief.
terra: Those with means nevertheless consent to remain behind and lose understanding through sealed hearts, another instance of satisfaction aimed at moral retreat.

terra: Hypocrites seek the believers' satisfaction by oaths, yet even human satisfaction cannot make Allah pleased with defiantly disobedient people; it breaks false assumed reciprocity between the two directions of rida.

luna: The section names mutual رضى and cites its formula; 9:100 applies the same “Allah pleased with them and they with Him” to the first emigrants, helpers, and those who follow them well. It shows the reciprocal state in a community. | terra: Allah's satisfaction with the first believers and their satisfaction with Him accompany prepared gardens, so reciprocal rida and a divine gift are explicitly bound together.
terra: A building founded on reverence and Allah's pleasure is contrasted with one founded on a crumbling brink, turning rida into the intended ground of effort and exposing its destructive opposite.
terra: Those pleased and settled with the worldly life direct rida toward what passes, illuminating by reversal the promised satisfaction attached to what Allah gives.
terra: Lot wishes he had strength against the crowd or could take refuge in a powerful support, using the āwā root for sought protection in a scene of exposed vulnerability.
terra: Joseph contrasts scattered lords with Allah الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ, locating irresistible mastery in the one God while he speaks from unjust human confinement.

luna: The source section says the dictionary branch of ء و ي can mean a heart turning tenderly toward someone; Joseph “took his brother close” (آوَىٰ إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ) and tells him not to grieve. It makes sheltering an intimate act of compassion toward a distressed person. | terra: Joseph takes his brother into his own lodging with آوَىٰ إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ and immediately tells him not to grieve, bringing refuge, familial love, and grief's easing into one act.

luna: The source section explicitly gives grief (الحزن) as a secondary dictionary sense of و ج د; Jacob’s eyes turn white from grief for Joseph (مِنَ الْحُزْنِ). It makes that hidden emotional face concrete as sorrow at separation. | terra: Jacob turns away in grief for Joseph until his eyes whiten, giving the section's dictionary statement that wajd can be grief a fully developed Quranic heart-scene.

luna: The source section names grief as a secondary dictionary sense of و ج د; Jacob says he complains of his anguish and grief only to God. This gives grief a direction toward God, rather than treating it as rejection of the one who suffers. | terra: Jacob says that he complains his anguish and grief only to Allah; this clarifies the grief that surrounds his sensory 'finding' of Joseph's scent in 12:94 and gives the source dictionary's grief sense a named direction.
terra: Jacob says he finds Joseph's scent before the reunion; وَجَدَ here is sensory, yet the finding is inseparable in context from the enduring love and grief developed around Joseph.
terra: Joseph takes his parents into his care and tells the family to enter Egypt in safety; reunion gives the root's sheltering act an affectionate family direction.
terra: After denying that alleged partners create anything, the ayah names Allah الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ; qahr belongs to the sole Creator, sharpening the limit on human overpowering.

terra: Abraham asks Allah to make people's hearts incline toward his vulnerable family and provide them fruits so they may be grateful; heartward turning and provision are joined as cause and response.
terra: All creation emerges before Allah الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ on the transformed earth, giving qahr its eschatological divine scale rather than the petty domination of an orphan.
terra: Allah removes all rancor from the garden-dwellers' breasts and seats them as brothers facing one another, so cleared hostility becomes reciprocal nearness.
terra: The one compelled outwardly while the heart remains secure in faith is excepted from blame, sharply distinguishing coerced action from the heart's actual willing direction.

luna: The section’s root ق ه ر is glossed as coercive taking; 17:34 repeats the rule not to approach an orphan’s property except in the best manner until maturity. This repeated command makes the consent and stewardship boundary explicit. | terra: The same ban on approaching orphan property except in the best way, followed by the demand to fulfill covenants, gives the section's emotional ethic a concrete legal edge.

luna: The section’s root ء و ي describes taking someone in; the youths “took refuge in the cave” (أَوَى الْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى الْكَهْفِ) and ask their Lord for mercy. Their threatened retreat gives the shelter image another concrete setting. | terra: The youths take refuge in the cave and ask their Lord for mercy and rightly prepared affairs, joining self-sought shelter to divine tenderness.

luna: The section’s root ء و ي is a word for sheltering; the youths tell one another فَأْوُوا إِلَى الْكَهْفِ, then say their Lord will spread mercy for them. It links refuge to the tender protection named in the section. | terra: The youths are told to take refuge in the cave, where their Lord will spread mercy and prepare ease for them; physical shelter becomes the site of tender divine provision.
terra: The Prophet is told that he will find no refuge apart from Allah; لَن تَجِدَ ... مُلْتَحَدًا brings the section's 'find' and 'shelter' motifs into one formulation.

luna: The section describes a heart turning tenderly toward another; 18:28 commands patience with those who call their Lord seeking His face and warns against turning one’s eyes away toward worldly adornment. It states the attentional choice that protects humble people from rejection.

terra: Allah preserves a treasure under the wall for two orphan boys until they reach maturity, explicitly calling this their Lord's mercy; divine shelter protects both vulnerable children and their property.

luna: The section names love as a secondary dictionary sense of و ج د and cites love bestowed on Moses; 19:96 says the Merciful will establish affection for those who believe and do good. It repeats the specific image of love given by God. | terra: The Merciful will appoint affection for those who believe and act rightly, another direct instance of love being divinely placed rather than self-generated.

luna: The source section identifies love as a secondary dictionary sense of و ج د; God says وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّي to Moses, the infant put into the water. The bestowed love is the stated counter-pole to aversion and accompanies protection in the same scene. | terra: Allah casts مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّي upon the exposed infant Moses; divinely placed love is the direct opposite pole to the hatred denied in 93:3, and it causes others to receive the vulnerable child.

luna: The section connects bestowed love for Moses with the exposed infant in 20:39; this adjacent ayah contributes his return to his mother so her eye may be comforted and she not grieve (وَلَا تَحْزَنَ). It completes the rescue with the mother’s relieved heart. | terra: This continuation of 20:39 returns Moses to his mother so that her eye may be cooled and she may not grieve, then recalls his rescue from distress; bestowed love culminates in relieved sorrow and care.
terra: Moses says that he hastened toward his Lord so that He might be pleased; movement, effort, and the sought direction of rida are explicit.

luna: The section quotes 20:130’s instruction to glorify God during the night and day’s ends, لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ. It links the same promised رضى to worship across the day’s turning points. | terra: The Prophet is told to endure speech and glorify through the night's hours and the day's edges لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ, making satisfaction an attained result across alternating times rather than an instantaneous feeling.
terra: Allah will admit the emigrants and slain believers into an entrance they will approve, another future divine giving whose result is their satisfaction.
terra: Allah shelters Mary and Jesus on secure high ground with flowing water, extending āwā to protection of a vulnerable mother and child.

terra: Those who love that Allah forgive them are told to pardon and overlook needy kin; hoped-for divine favor is converted into merciful treatment of a vulnerable other, as satisfaction in the section becomes care for the orphan.
terra: The prohibition on compelling women into prostitution when they desire chastity is a precise boundary against exploiting another without her rida for material gain.
terra: Allah promises to exchange the believers' fear for security and establish for them the religion He has approved, joining divine rida, shelter-like security, and a bestowed change of state.

luna: “The source section names ق ل ي and glosses it as شدة البغض; Lot calls himself among مِنَ الْقَالِينَ of their deed, giving the same severe aversion a precise object: the act, not its people. | terra: This is the Quran's other use of the q-l-y root, and Lot's لِعَمَلِكُم مِّنَ الْقَالِينَ directs loathing explicitly at his people's acts rather than leaving its object as a person.

luna: The section recalls Moses as the baby placed in water when love is cast upon him in 20:39; 28:7 retells his mother’s fearful act of placing him in the river and God’s promise to return him and make him a messenger. It supplies the vulnerable-child scene behind that bestowed love. | terra: Moses's mother is told to nurse him, cast him into the river when afraid, and neither fear nor grieve because he will be returned; this sets the emotional peril answered by the love and shelter of 20:39.

terra: Pharaoh's household picks up Moses even though he will become an enemy and grief to them; this supplies the paradoxical hostile setting in which the love described in 20:39 moves Pharaoh's wife to protect him in 28:9.

luna: The section’s love pole is God’s love cast upon threatened Moses; in this retelling Pharaoh’s wife asks that the child not be killed and calls him a coolness of eyes for them (قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّي وَلَكَ). Care arises even in the enemy’s household, complicating the scene of enmity. | terra: Pharaoh's wife calls the found infant a comfort of the eye, forbids his killing, and hopes to adopt him; this shows the love cast on Moses in 20:39 turning a heart toward protecting him.
terra: The mother's heart becomes empty and is then bound firm by Allah, making divine action upon a distressed heart part of the infant-refuge scene.
terra: Moses is prevented from accepting other nurses until his sister directs the household back toward his own family, the immediate means by which grief will turn into relief.

luna: The section cites God’s love for Moses in 20:39; this parallel account contributes his return to his mother “so her eye may be comforted and she not grieve” (كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ). It completes the image with grief relieved by reunion. | terra: Moses is returned to his mother so her eye may be cooled and she may not grieve, making emotional restoration the outcome of the infant's divinely managed refuge.
terra: Moses finds two women holding back their flock, recognizes their vulnerable position, and asks about it; an ordinary وَجَدَ immediately opens into attentive concern for others.
terra: Moses waters for the women and then turns to his Lord in need, completing the compassionate action prompted by the finding in 28:23.
terra: Allah places affection and mercy between spouses so that each finds repose with the other; the emotion is bestowed, relational, and reciprocal rather than merely private.

terra: The arrangement is said to be likelier to cool the wives' eyes, keep them from grieving, and make all of them satisfied with what the Prophet gives them; gift, grief's removal, and rida are joined in one relational scene.
terra: The warning that there is no god but Allah الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ makes overpowering an attribute of unique divinity, against which the human prohibition becomes legible.
terra: In rejecting any divine child, the ayah names Allah الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ; absolute qahr is paired with divine uniqueness, not human possession of another.

terra: Allah does not approve disbelief for His servants but approves gratitude for them; rida is aimed at a response rather than indiscriminately at persons, paralleling Lot's hatred of deeds rather than people.
terra: On the day all are exposed, dominion is declared to belong to Allah الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ, the ultimate boundary for every human claim to coercive mastery.
terra: Those who avoid grave sins forgive when angered, showing the anger face of the heart governed into merciful action rather than coercion.

luna: The section explicitly gives رضى as opposite to displeasure; 47:28 says the condemned followed what angered God and disliked His رضوان (وَكَرِهُوا رِضْوَانَهُ). The verse places both poles in one account of a chosen direction. | terra: They follow what angers Allah and hate His رضوان, placing divine anger and satisfaction at opposed ends and showing a heart deliberately oriented away from the pleasing end.

luna: The section describes a feeling removed from God in 93:3 and a satisfaction given in 93:5; 48:18 says God was pleased with the believers at the pledge under the tree, knowing what was in their hearts, then sent tranquility. It supplies a concrete instance of divine رضى meeting an inward commitment. | terra: Allah is pleased with the believers, knows what is in their hearts, and sends tranquility and a near victory; divine rida, the heart's state, and subsequent giving form one causal sequence.
terra: The Prophet's companions seek bounty and satisfaction from Allah, with the marks of sustained worship visible on them; effort is directed toward divine rida.

terra: Allah makes faith beloved and beautifies it in hearts while making disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful; it is the clearest parallel to feelings being placed in the heart and aimed at their proper objects.
terra: The passing competition of worldly life is set against forgiveness and رضوان from Allah, placing enduring rida beyond what withers and sharpening the surah's latter-over-former horizon.
terra: Allah places compassion and mercy in the hearts of Jesus's followers; this parallels the source dictionary's āwā as a heart turning toward another and becoming tender.

luna: The section says رضى can run in both directions; 58:22 says Allah is pleased with a people whose hearts He has strengthened in faith, and they are pleased with Him (رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ). It makes the inward orientation and reciprocal relation explicit. | terra: This ayah gathers the section's whole emotional arc: لَا تَجِدُ introduces a finding, affection is bounded by its proper object, faith is set in hearts, and رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ makes satisfaction reciprocal.
terra: The dispossessed emigrants seek bounty and pleasure from Allah after losing homes and property; hardship and active fidelity orient them toward divine rida.

luna: The section’s dictionary glosses for و ج د include love and heart-states, and its note on ء و ي describes a heart turning toward someone. This verse joins welcome for emigrants, love for them, and finding no need in one’s breast; it shows affection enacted as hospitality and selfless care. | terra: The hosts find no need or resentment in their breasts concerning what the emigrants are given and prefer them over themselves; an inward finding, another's gift, and generous affection converge.
terra: Later believers ask Allah to remove rancor from their hearts toward believers, making the removal of a hostile feeling from the heart an explicit divine gift.
terra: The believers are rebuked for casting affection toward active enemies; it is the negative counterpart to 60:7 and makes the proper object and direction of love the issue.

luna: The section moves from an image of aversion to love and رضى; 60:7 says God may place affection between believers and people with whom they are at enmity. It gives a specific divine reversal from hostility toward affection. | terra: Allah may place affection between the believers and those they have treated as enemies, making a divinely caused turn from hostility to love visible.
terra: The Prophet is corrected for prohibiting what Allah made lawful while seeking his wives' satisfaction; human rida is a real aim but has a revealed boundary.
terra: عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ turns the r-d-w root into the quality of the rewarded life itself, a secondary usage that makes promised satisfaction an encompassing condition.
terra: The messenger declares that no one can protect him from Allah and that he will find no refuge apart from Him, again coupling finding with the direction of ultimate shelter.

luna: The section’s secondary gloss for و ج د includes love; 76:8 describes feeding an orphan عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ. The pronoun’s referent is read as the food or God, but either reading places love beside concrete care for the orphan. | terra: They feed the needy, the orphan, and the captive despite love of the food, turning the heart's governing love into care for vulnerable recipients.
terra: The feeders seek only Allah's face and want neither recompense nor thanks, specifying the direction of the love-driven orphan care in 76:8.

luna: The section’s dictionary note for ء و ي evokes a heart turning compassionately toward someone; 80:1 opens with a frown and turning away from a visitor, the opposite bodily and emotional movement.

luna: The section pairs sheltering an orphan with not dominating him; 80:2 identifies the person from whom the speaker turned away in 80:1 as a blind man who came to him. This row specifies the visitor’s vulnerability.

luna: The section’s image contrasts care for the vulnerable with rejection; 80:5 introduces the person who considers himself self-sufficient as the one receiving attention in the exchange begun at 80:1. It supplies the contrasting social position.

luna: The section’s heart-turning image includes compassion for someone vulnerable; 80:6 says attention is given to the self-sufficient man, completing the redirection described in 80:1 while the needy visitor is neglected.

luna: The section says the heart can turn toward someone with tenderness; 80:8 introduces the other visitor, who comes eagerly to the Prophet in the same scene. His active approach makes the subsequent neglect in 80:10 concrete.

luna: The section’s emotional image attends to the heart’s state; 80:9 describes the eager visitor of 80:8 as fearing God. This identifies the spiritual orientation of the person who is nevertheless neglected in 80:10.

luna: The section commands that the orphan not be subjected to harm; 80:10 says the speaker is distracted from the God-fearing visitor introduced in 80:8–9. It completes the scene of turning away from a vulnerable petitioner.
terra: A face in the hereafter is satisfied with its striving, linking completed effort to a later state of rida.

luna: The section joins a promised gift to the recipient’s رضى; 89:15 depicts someone treating abundant provision as proof that God has honored him. The following correction in 89:17 matters: this verse contributes the mistaken equation between wealth and worth.

luna: The section’s movement from divine displeasure to رضى is about the heart’s response; 89:16 gives the opposite material condition, restricted provision, and the person concludes that God has humiliated him. The passage’s correction in 89:17 exposes that conclusion as false.

luna: The section’s orphan image joins being received and protected to the command not to dominate; 89:17 rebukes people for failing to honor the orphan (لَّا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ). It identifies withholding dignity as the opposite of shelter. | terra: The accusation that they do not honor the orphan is the behavioral opposite of a heart softened by having received divine care.

luna: The section connects divine sheltering with the command not to oppress an orphan; after 89:17 rebukes failure to honor the orphan, 89:18 adds failure to urge feeding the poor. This row broadens the same neglect of vulnerable people. | terra: Failure to urge one another to feed the poor continues the orphan-neglect scene and identifies the absence of shared compassionate action between 89:17 and the greedy taking in 89:19.

luna: The section’s dictionary note for ق ه ر defines coercive taking without consent; 89:19 condemns devouring inheritance in a single, consuming manner. Beside the rebuke about the orphan in 89:17, it shows how taking can replace care. | terra: Greedily consuming inheritance enacts the taking-from-the-vulnerable without their rida that the section draws out of the prohibition of qahr.

luna: The section’s secondary dictionary gloss for و ج د includes الحب; 89:20 says people love wealth with great love, after the passage has condemned neglect of the orphan and devouring inheritance. It sets possessive love against the section’s love expressed as care and giving. | terra: Excessive love of wealth explains the misdirected heart behind the preceding neglect and consumption of the orphan's due.

luna: The section’s emotional image ends with return to God in رضى at 89:28; this preceding ayah identifies the addressed person as the tranquil soul (النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ), supplying the heart-state from which that return is spoken.

luna: The section quotes this return to God as a state of رضى; 89:28 addresses the soul to return to its Lord رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً, joining the servant’s contentment to being accepted by God. | terra: رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً depicts the soul returning to its Lord both satisfied and approved, joining heartward return with the two-sided rida developed in the section.

luna: The section’s note on ء و ي describes pity and a softened heart; 90:14 places feeding on a day of severe hunger at the start of the steep-pass scene. The next ayah, 90:15, specifies a near-relative orphan as one recipient, while this row contributes the urgent act of feeding.

luna: The section’s note on ء و ي describes pity and a softened heart toward someone; in the steep-pass sequence, 90:15 identifies the recipient as a near-relative orphan (يَتِيمًا ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ), while 90:14 supplies feeding during hunger. The row makes the orphan a specific object of active compassion. | terra: Feeding an orphaned relative on a day of hunger gives a concrete positive form to the compassionate turn toward an orphan.

luna: The section’s heart-softening image is enacted toward a vulnerable person; 90:16 identifies another recipient in the steep-pass passage as a poor person in the dust. Alongside the orphan in 90:15, it extends care to the materially exposed.

luna: The section pairs a promise of giving with رضى; 92:18 introduces the person who gives wealth to purify himself, whose promised outcome is stated in 92:21. This row supplies the effortful giving behind that parallel promise. | terra: This neighbour identifies the promised recipient of 92:21 as one who gives his wealth to purify himself, letting the near-identical satisfaction promise be read as the result of a prior gift.

luna: The section says رضى may be brought about after effort; 92:20 says the giver seeks only the face of his Lord, while 92:21 gives the promise that he will be pleased. This row identifies the aim behind the giving. | terra: The giver seeks only the face of his Lord Most High; this specifies the upward direction of the effort that culminates in وَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ.

luna: The section directly compares its promise وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ with the preceding surah’s وَ لَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ. The parallel also changes the stance: 93:5 addresses the Prophet as recipient of God’s giving, while 92:21 describes the giver who becomes satisfied. | terra: وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ repeats the promise structure of 93:5 almost word for word, but promises satisfaction to the self-purifying giver described in the preceding ayat.
terra: The command to labor when free supplies the exertion immediately before the heartward direction of 94:8, paralleling the section's claim that rida is brought through effort.
terra: The same prophetic addressee is told to direct his longing toward his Lord, an explicit command for the heart's orientation after remembered divine gifts.

luna: The section explicitly says رضى can be mutual and quotes this formula; 98:8 says Allah is pleased with them and they with Him (رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ), adding that this is for one who fears his Lord. | terra: رَّضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ names divine-human satisfaction in both directions, the Quranic realization of the section's mutual form of rida.
terra: The one whose scales are heavy enters عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ; rida-language again names the life granted after measured deeds.

luna: The section sets God’s sheltering of the orphan in 93:6 beside the ban on subjugating him in 93:9; 107:2 describes the one who harshly repels an orphan (يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ). It gives the direct contrary conduct the section’s image rules out. | terra: Violently repelling the orphan is the direct enacted opposite of āwā as shelter and tender heartward return.

luna: After 107:2 describes repelling an orphan, 107:3 adds failure to urge feeding the poor. The section’s sheltering and non-oppression image thus sits within a wider rebuke of withholding care from the vulnerable. | terra: Refusal to encourage feeding the poor continues the repulsion of the orphan in 107:2, showing that a hard heart withholds both personal shelter and communal concern.
